content.text: No audit, inspection, verification or records-examination provision appears anywhere in the Agreement.

input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: The Agreement grants Kubient no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right over the Customer (AP). Full-text searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verif" return nothing, and a read of the entire Master Services Agreement confirms no such right: fees flow from Kubient to AP under a revenue-share with sequential liability (p0023), so there is no usage or underpayment for Kubient to audit. The only access-related obligation is AP's agreement in Section 1 to provide reasonable access, support and cooperation for Kubient to deliver the Services (p0001) — that is a service-enablement cooperation covenant, not an audit or verification right, and it confers no right to examine AP's books or systems. The absence of any vendor audit right is more favourable to us than the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so there is nothing to limit and no redline is warranted. We would resist any attempt to introduce audit or system-access language in an Exhibit or amendment without the preferred parameters.
